title: Edmund Washington and Ida's sister subbing in his group
summary: Allen asks about saxophonist Edmund Washington; Ida describes him and says her sister played with him and she once filled in.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Uh... Did you ever know a fella named Edmund Washington?
He's a big, fat fella now. I don't know. You know him, don't you?

I wanted to see the one who came here from, uh... Did he come from New Orleans over here to play? Mm-hmm. Yes, I remember him. But, uh, I'll tell you what, my sister, other sister, played with them. Mm-hmm. I tell you who, uh, you know this guy, what pop, they call him? Oh, that's Kid Ernest. No, that's, you know, he come here with Kid Ernest, I'm trying to say now. But not Kid Ernest. It was one of them big men that came in with him, Edmund, they went out to shorty, they played things out to shorty one, just a long time ago. It was a great big fella. Brown-skinned fella got a big stomach sticking out like that.

That's him, I know. That's what that's ever all. That's what that's ever all. Yeah, my sister played with him, Bob. I went to work one time in her place, because she got a booze there and couldn't go, so I went to work one time, but I never played too much with that bunch. She got a what?
You know Ed Dick. What's a booze-an?
Yeah, too much of that booze-an.
A little booze-an party. Oh, yeah.
And she went over to make the job, and I played in the place or something.
